Delete an object by its ID.



By default, deletion will fail if the object has dependents (objects that
reference it).

Use --unlink-references to remove this ID from dependents' reference fields
(CASCADE_NULLIFY-style), then delete.

Use --cascade to delete the object and all its dependents recursively.

Do not combine --unlink-references with --cascade.

  Delete an object (fails if it has dependents)
  zqk delete ITEM-626
  Drop references from dependents (nullify refs), then delete
  zqk delete CRIT-002 --unlink-references
  Delete with cascade (deletes object and all dependents)
  zqk delete ITEM-626 --cascade
  Dry-run to see what would be deleted
  zqk delete ITEM-626 --cascade --dry-run

Usage:
  zqk object delete <id> [flags]

Aliases:
  delete, rm, remove

Flags:
      --cascade                 Delete object and all objects that reference it
      --columns string          Override column widths for table output (format: field:width)
      --dry-run                 Show what would be done without actually doing it
  -f, --format string           Output format (table, json, jsonl, yaml, csv, json-rpc, stream, agent-prompt, semantic-link) (default "table")
      --ignore-scheduler-down   Ignore scheduler down warning/lockdown
  -o, --output string           Write output to file
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress non-essential output
      --timeout duration        Timeout for command execution (0 = auto-calculate)
      --unlink-references       Strip this ID from dependents' reference fields, then delete (does not delete dependent objects)
  -v, --verbose                 Verbose output

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
